To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the four-element wind-kessel model with all its elements (compliance, resistance, characteristic impedance, and total arterial inertance) has a hemodynamic meaning and is superior to the traditional three-element model as a lumped parameter model of the entire arterial system.

the four-element wind-kessel, with an inertance in parallel with the impedance, is superior to a three-element windkessell as a lumped parameter model of the entire system, or as a model to derive vascular properties.

the four-element wind-kessel model, with a total arterial inertance in parallel to the characteristic impedance, is superior to a three-element windkessell model for the prediction of arterial pressure from flow and for the estimation of arterial compliance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new model of the arterial tree that is more realistic and accurate than existing models.
a better understanding of the hemodynamic behavior of the systemic tree and with a better estimation of vascular properties.
a new element of the wind-kessel model, total arterial inertance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the four-element wind-kessel is the best lumped-parameter model for arterial hemodynamics, and that it is superior to the classical three-element windkessell.
the four-element wind-kessel model, with its four elements, is a more accurate model for the systemic arterial tree than the three-element wind-kessel.
the four-element wind-kessel model is the best available lumped-parameter model for the arterial tree.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
total arterial inertance is an important fourth element in the windkessel.
the four-element wind kessel model is the simplest model that is accurate enough to be applied in clinical practice.
the windkessel is a useful model of the systemic tree, but that it should be extended to four elements to be a more realistic representation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
total arterial inertance is an important element in a lumped-parameter windkessel model of the entire arterial system.
total arterial compliance and characteristic impedance can be accurately determined from a single pressure and flow signal using the four-element model.
total arterial inertance is an important parameter that should be included in any lumped-parameter model for the systemic tree.
